section_summary: This section opens with nine SCAP industrial inventory summaries covering Japanese fuel, vehicles, metals, handicrafts, building materials, machinery, electrical equipment, and mining. Later documents concern Indian technical missions and supplies, access to Japanese industrial information, restitution of a Hong Kong lathe, and proposals for Japan’s industrial disarmament. The section ends partway through a National Engineers Committee report.

subfiles.title: Transmission of Summaries of Industrial Inventories
subfiles.about: Transmits duplicate copies of industrial inventories 15–23.
subfiles.summary: Encloses inventories 15–23 and notes that inventories 8–14 were unavailable in Tokyo.

subfiles.title: Last of the Summaries of Industrial Inventories
subfiles.from: United States Army Forces, Pacific, Public Relations Office
subfiles.about: Introduces the final nine inventory summaries prepared for Ambassador Pauley.
subfiles.summary: Identifies their SCAP authors and Japanese government and industry sources.

subfiles.title: Industrial Inventory No. 15: Synthetic Oil
subfiles.about: Summarizes Japanese synthetic fuel production and storage.
subfiles.summary: Reports output by fuel type and inventories civilian and naval storage, including damaged facilities at Kure and Yokosuka.

subfiles.title: Industrial Inventory No. 16: Automotive
subfiles.about: Reviews passenger car and truck manufacture in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Details Toyota and Nissan output and capacity, wartime production declines, and shortages obstructing commercial production.

subfiles.title: Industrial Inventory No. 17: Non-Ferrous Metals
subfiles.about: Surveys Japanese copper, zinc, lead, tin, and ferro-alloy industries.
subfiles.summary: Compiles production, imports, mine and refinery capacities, and major producers. It traces heavy prewar reliance on foreign metal supplies and wartime shifts toward domestic, colonial, and scrap sources. The summary also records tin stocks and ferro-alloy output.

subfiles.title: Industrial Inventory No. 18: Handicraft Industry
subfiles.about: Estimates the export potential of Japanese handicrafts.
subfiles.summary: Covers ceramics, lacquerware, toys, pearls, cloisonné, bamboo goods, lanterns, and glassware, including war damage and restart prospects.

subfiles.title: Industrial Inventory No. 19: Building Materials
subfiles.about: Surveys production and capacity for Japanese building materials.
subfiles.summary: Reviews plaster, glass, cement, sand, gravel, and lime, noting shortages and falling wartime output.

subfiles.title: Industrial Inventory No. 20: Machinery Other Than Machine Tools
subfiles.about: Estimates Japanese machinery manufacturing capacity across many branches.
subfiles.summary: Explains that destroyed records and secret military production make estimates uncertain. It lists factory numbers and potential output for engines, boilers, pumps, construction machinery, textile machinery, bearings, and other equipment. Several capacities depend on reconversion from war production.

subfiles.title: Industrial Inventory No. 21: Iron and Steel Forgings and Castings
subfiles.about: Reports production and capacity for steel forgings and metal castings.
subfiles.summary: Compares historical output and factory counts with estimated current capacity in steel and iron forging and casting.

subfiles.title: Industrial Inventory No. 22: Heavy Electrical Machinery
subfiles.about: Estimates capacity for generators, turbines, transformers, and switching equipment.
subfiles.summary: Reports that six companies account for most Japanese heavy electrical equipment production.

subfiles.title: Industrial Inventory No. 23: Other Mining
subfiles.about: Reviews production and supply of selected Japanese minerals.
subfiles.summary: Covers gold, silver, sulphur, pyrite, chromium, manganese, nickel, tungsten, and molybdenum. It compares historical production and imports with likely peacetime supply, noting depleted deposits, wartime subsidies, and dependence on imported minerals.

subfiles.title: Indian Request for a Technical Mission to Japan
subfiles.about: Requests permission for Indian experts to study industries in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Proposes studies of fertilizers, textiles, ceramics, newsprint, steel rolling, rice cultivation, fisheries, and industrial organization. India requests SCAP approval and facilities.

subfiles.title: Reply to Indian Request for a Technical Mission
subfiles.about: Defers consideration of India’s proposed industrial mission.
subfiles.summary: Suggests discussing the visit after governments agree on reparations procedures and foreign inspection arrangements.

subfiles.title: Transmission of Report on the Oji Paper Manufacturing Company
subfiles.about: Forwards a Civil Censorship Detachment report on Oji Paper.
subfiles.summary: Encloses the report dated November 29, 1945.

subfiles.title: Special Report: Oji Paper Manufacturing Company, Ltd.
subfiles.about: Examines Oji Paper’s production, distribution, finances, and influence over newsprint.
subfiles.summary: Describes Oji’s dominant share of Japanese paper production, its mills and subsidiaries, wartime output decline, and its place in newsprint rationing. It lists newspaper allocations, finances, and company management.

subfiles.title: Request to Investigate Japanese Scientific and Industrial Developments
subfiles.about: Seeks State Department approval for specialists to survey Japanese technology.
subfiles.summary: Proposes a small group of specialists to identify developments worth further investigation.

subfiles.title: Reply on Technical Information Missions to Japan
subfiles.about: Sets conditions for proposed technical information missions.
subfiles.summary: Accepts missions in principle, subject to occupation rules, security screening, publication, and equitable Allied access.

subfiles.title: Further Proposal for Scientific and Industrial Investigation
subfiles.about: Urges a modest investigation of Japanese scientific and industrial advances.
subfiles.summary: Proposes roughly twenty specialist investigators whose reports would be distributed through the Publication Board.

subfiles.title: Indian Inquiry About Mill Stores and Dyes
subfiles.about: Requests information on Japanese mill stores, machinery, bobbins, and dyes for India.
subfiles.summary: India offers to purchase available supplies if they cannot be allocated as reparations and asks for an urgent reply.

subfiles.title: Reply on Japanese Mill Stores and Dyes
subfiles.about: Relays SCAP’s preliminary findings on textile supplies for India.
subfiles.summary: Only limited spare parts are available; rubber rollers are unavailable, while dyes can be made in some colors.

subfiles.title: Renewed Indian Request for a Technical Mission
subfiles.about: Renews India’s request to send technical experts to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Explains that the proposed industrial study serves India’s development program and is separate from reparations inspection.

subfiles.title: Clayton Routing Note on Indian Mission
subfiles.about: Requests a favorable effort and appropriate reply on India’s proposed mission.
subfiles.summary: Clayton urges finding a way to permit India’s small mission.

subfiles.title: Acknowledgment to Sir Girja Bajpai
subfiles.about: Acknowledges the request for an Indian technical mission.
subfiles.summary: Promises to examine the request and reply shortly.

subfiles.title: Decision on Indian Technical Mission
subfiles.about: Conveys SCAP’s preference to postpone the Indian mission.
subfiles.summary: Cites unresolved economic questions, scarce accommodation, and pending Far Eastern Commission procedures.

subfiles.title: Notice of Restitution of Taikoo Lathe
subfiles.about: Reports arrangements to return a Taikoo Dockyard lathe.
subfiles.summary: Says Japan was directed to deliver the identified machine to a British representative at Kure.

subfiles.title: Request to Cable SCAP About Industrial Equipment Restitution
subfiles.about: Asks the War Department to send a restitution cable to SCAP.
subfiles.summary: Encloses the draft cable and requests a copy of the dispatched message.

subfiles.title: Draft Cable to SCAP on Taikoo Lathe
subfiles.about: Requests restitution of equipment taken from Taikoo Dockyard in Hong Kong.
subfiles.summary: Describes the lathe, motors, identifying marks, and location at Mitsui’s Tamano yard.

subfiles.title: Request for Strategic Bombing Survey Studies
subfiles.from: Office of Far Eastern Affairs, Department of State
subfiles.about: Forwards a request for studies of Japan’s industrial economy.
subfiles.summary: Asks the War Department to consider sharing Strategic Bombing Survey studies with the Far Eastern Commission.

subfiles.title: Interim Reply on Taikoo Lathe Restitution
subfiles.about: Acknowledges Britain’s request for return of the Taikoo lathe.
subfiles.summary: States that the request has been cabled to SCAP and that further action will be reported.

subfiles.title: British Request for Restitution of Taikoo Lathe
subfiles.about: Requests release of a looted lathe to its Hong Kong owner.
subfiles.summary: Supplies the machine’s specifications, marks, maker, motors, and reported location at a Mitsui shipyard.

subfiles.title: Reply on British Industrial Policy Conclusions for Japan
subfiles.about: Responds to British proposals for Japan’s permitted industrial level.
subfiles.summary: Suggests submitting the proposals to the Far Eastern Commission and notes that final United States views remain under development.

subfiles.title: Routing Slip on Draft Letter
subfiles.about: Flags a typographical error in a letter’s opening.
subfiles.summary: Requests correction and Hamilton’s initial.

subfiles.title: Corrected Location of Taikoo Lathe
subfiles.about: Corrects the reported location of the looted lathe.
subfiles.summary: Gives Mitsui Shipbuilding Yard, Tamano, Okayama Prefecture, as the location.

subfiles.title: File Note on Revised Letter to John C. Green
subfiles.about: Explains revision of a proposed reply about technical information missions.
subfiles.summary: Notes that an earlier draft was withdrawn because German and Japanese policies could not be sharply separated.

subfiles.title: Japanese War Procurement Policies
subfiles.about: Records an interview about Japanese wartime procurement and contracting.
subfiles.summary: Taguchi describes government factories, compelled expansion, financing, advance payments, contract termination, and treatment of manufacturers’ profits.

subfiles.title: Memorandum on National Engineers Committee Report
subfiles.about: Discusses clearance, printing, and release of an industrial disarmament report.
subfiles.summary: Records plans to submit the independent engineers’ report to the Secretaries of State, War, and Navy, arrange security clearance, and coordinate publicity. Barnett notes that its proposed industrial controls are stricter than current State Department thinking.

subfiles.title: Cover Letter on Engineers’ Report
subfiles.about: Forwards a copy of Proctor’s letter to General Echols.
subfiles.summary: Explains that the enclosed letter seeks decisions about the engineers’ forthcoming report.

subfiles.title: Plans for Industrial Disarmament Report
subfiles.about: Seeks advice on review, printing, and public release of the engineers’ report.
subfiles.summary: Invites Echols and Hilldring to the committee meeting and requests prompt instructions on printing and press arrangements.

subfiles.title: Report on the Industrial Disarmament of Japan
subfiles.from: National Engineers Committee, Engineers Joint Council
subfiles.to: Secretaries of State, War, and Navy
subfiles.about: Proposes lasting controls on Japan’s industrial capacity for war.
subfiles.summary: The opening states the committee’s mandate and argues for durable controls that preserve a functioning civilian economy. It discusses Japanese resources, regional trade, and the need for simple controls over primary war materials. The report identifies mineral and metal industries, heavy chemicals, fuel, and electrical power as principal targets, then begins its mineral-industry analysis.
